records.source_product_id: Azua-Bustos et al. (2020), Inhabited subsurface wet smectites in the hyperarid core of the Atacama Desert
records.summary: The study reports active microbial communities in wet smectite-rich soil layers about 30–40 cm below the surface. Sensors in one studied pit recorded about 78% relative humidity (water activity 0.780) in the clay layer during measurement periods in 2018–2019.

measurements.name: Relative humidity in a subsurface clay layer
measurements.uncertainty: One instrumented pit is described; this is not a regional average or a current measurement.

measurements.name: Water activity in a subsurface clay layer
measurements.uncertainty: Study-specific sampled layer; water activity does not mean water is recoverable or usable as a resource.

records.spatial_relation: The paper gives a study coordinate near Yungay; the ENOM candidate is a broad regional point about 60 km away. Treat this as nearby regional context, not an observation at the candidate coordinate.
records.use_limit: Earth microbial and moisture context only. It is not evidence of life or biosignatures on Mars.

records.study_region: Haughton impact structure, Devon Island, Canadian High Arctic
records.source_product_id: Fike et al. (2003), Heterotrophic microbial colonization of impact-shocked rocks from Haughton impact structure
records.summary: The study reports 27 heterotrophic bacterial isolates from impact-shocked gneiss and host breccia samples collected in the Haughton impact structure.

measurements.name: Heterotrophic bacterial isolates reported from sampled rocks
measurements.uncertainty: A count of isolates from the paper's rock samples; it is not a measure of abundance across the crater.

records.spatial_relation: The article identifies the Haughton impact structure but does not provide a coordinate for the sampled rocks in its abstract. Link at crater-region level only.
records.use_limit: Earth sample evidence only; it does not indicate life on Mars or elsewhere.

records.study_region: Taylor Valley water tracks, McMurdo Dry Valleys, Antarctica
records.source_product_id: George et al. (2021), Antarctic Water Tracks: Microbial Community Responses to Variation in Soil Moisture, pH, and Salinity
records.temporal_coverage: Taylor Valley samples collected during the 2012–2013 austral summer
records.summary: The study compares microbial communities in seasonally wetted water tracks with nearby dry soils in Taylor Valley and reports differences in community composition associated with moisture, salinity, and pH.
records.spatial_relation: Sample coordinates are within the broad McMurdo Dry Valleys candidate region; they do not represent every valley or soil type.
records.use_limit: Published ecological context, not a standardized site-wide measurement or a score for planetary habitability.
